name: IMD (International Institute for Management Development)

program.note: Class profile PDF: 'a 12-month leadership-focused journey'. Local copy: research/sources/imd-class-profile-2026.pdf

tuition_total.cohort: page current on read date (installments, scholarships deadline 'throughout 2026')

mandatory_fees_total.note: Additional mandatory fees: pre-program course, travel & accommodation for IMD-organized projects, coaching, books, lunches on campus days, relocation & visa help. Fees exclusive of VAT/indirect taxes. Installments 10,000 + 22,500 + 45,000 + 20,000 = 97,500.

living_budget_total.note: 'The average for a single person is CHF 36,000' based on MBA feedback and budgets required by Swiss authorities.

scholarship.note: '48% of students received a scholarship from IMD'; '>50% of our scholarships are awarded to women'. No average amount published.

base_salary.note: Average annualised TOTAL compensation (not base), nominal USD at August 2026 FX; school states it equated to approx. CHF 110,000. PPP-adjusted figure: 176,719 international dollars (the '$180k median salary (USD PPP)' banner on the career page is a rounded marketing figure; the PDF says average).

employment.note: Salaries are mean annualised total compensation in nominal USD (first column) and PPP international dollars (second column) per the PDF; column mapping deduced from page 1 ($176,719 = PPP) and footnote ($136,940 = approx. CHF 110,000). Geography % on page 1 (Americas 7, Europe 71, Asia 15, Middle East & Africa 7) – the two 7% values are adjacent in the text extraction, harmless since equal. Career page also states '92% switch role, industry, and/or geography' (https://www.imd.org/degree/mba/career/development/). No employer list in the PDF.

profile.note: GMAT 615 = 'Average GMAT/GMAC score' on participants page (GMAT Focus scale presumed, not stated). Women 34% and 90 students from the class profile PDF. Share of non-Swiss students not published.

rankings_cited.note: Third-party extract of the FT table (tied 30th with Fudan); FT.com not read.

notes: IMD publishes average total compensation, not median base. Exclude from median-based comparisons or flag as mean total comp.
